utterances.text: Does that refresh your recollection about that particular commission?

utterances.speaker: ANDREJA MILOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, absolutely. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us what that was about?

utterances.speaker: ANDREJA MILOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: This was a particular event marking a particular anniversary. This honourary committee never held a single meeting. I was appointed, I guess, as one of the people who had helped Aleksinac in some matters, and I did not even attend the event itself. In my view, this is more of a -- well, there was some committee that prepared this and people who were doing that. I was on the honourary committee. Of course, I had been appointed, but not a single session of this committee was held; at least, I did not take part in a single session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And on the persons who are members with you, it also included General Pavkovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREJA MILOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And Mrs. Markovic?

utterances.speaker: ANDREJA MILOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you're listed as being a member of JUL; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREJA MILOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I'm not denying that. General Pavkovic hails from Aleksinac, and that was one of the criteria.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, when you became appointed to this position for coordinating things in Kosovo, how did it first -- how did that first come about? Were you approached and asked if you were willing to do this job, or were you nominated? Did you volunteer? How did you get that job?

utterances.speaker: ANDREJA MILOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The job of coordinator of state organs is one I got in the following way: The prime minister, Mirjanovic, invited me to his office and asked me whether I would wish to work in Kosovo and Metohija as coordinator of the state organs. The reason for my particular engagement, as he explained it to me then, lie in the fact that he had enormous trust in me. That was the result of my previous work in the government, and also due to the fact that I had vast experience in conducting affairs as far as municipalities and districts are concerned, because I have already pointed out that I was president of a municipality for 12 years, that is to say, I served three terms of office; that is to say, that I was very well-versed in economic matters, financial, and so on. I had exceptional energy for travel, work. I never kept strict working hours. In the government, I would start working at 7.00 in the morning and working hours started from 9.00 a.m., and that was a recommendation in his eyes when he suggested that I be coordinator. I thought about it briefly, and I accepted to go knowing what the problems were, and I knew that quite simply there was work to be done there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, can you find a suitable place to interrupt?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I can certainly see that, sir. You certainly seem to have a lot of energy and more than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think this would be a good time for us to break for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Just a little question. What was the status of the coordinator, please? Could you, sir, answer this: What was the status in terms of government hierarchy? What was your status? Were you equal to a minister or equal to a mayor or what would be the status? And were you paid for this job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My earnings came in my capacity as president of the Committee for Dealing with Natural Disasters. That is a government organ; and to be quite honest, I didn't put any questions because that's the way I worked during my life. It was important for me to work. I spent most of my time getting things done for my own area, but I accepted this in view of the fact that it was necessary to work down there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We're short of time at this stage. Could you deal with the specific question, please, about where you stood so far as status is concerned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My status was coordinator of the work of the state organs. It did not have a particular rank, but it was held in high regard, if I can put it that way, briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosavljevic, this courtroom, regrettably, is required by another case this afternoon, so we have to end our proceedings at this stage. That means that you will have to return tomorrow to continue your evidence. Tomorrow, we have what's commonly known as the graveyard slot. We are sitting in the afternoon on tomorrow, Friday, so your evidence will continue at 2.15 p.m. tomorrow. Meanwhile, it's vital that you do not discuss the evidence in the case with anyone. You can discuss whatever else you like with whoever you like, but no discussion whatsoever of the evidence. Please now leave the courtroom with the usher and return here to recommence at 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 24th day of August, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
